topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This topic frames the lecture series by introducing the course objectives, scope, and key learning outcomes.

topics.label: Biological foundations of cancer development and tissue modeling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer arises from accumulated genetic alterations and disrupted tissue differentiation programs, alongside the experimental models used to study these cellular behaviors.

topics.label: Pathology and progression of tumor invasion and metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the histological and pathological mechanisms through which localized tumors invade surrounding tissues and metastasize to distant organs.

topics.label: Tumor classification, nomenclature, and clinical pathophysiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the standard naming conventions for neoplasms and explain the physiological mechanisms by which benign and malignant growths cause illness and death.

topics.label: Cancer epidemiology and comparative oncology across species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the incidence and patterns of tumor occurrence across human tissues and diverse multicellular taxa.

topics.label: Clinical presentation, symptoms, and cancer screening approaches
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the clinical signs of tumors and the specific screening modalities used to detect early-stage and pre-malignant lesions.

topics.label: Lecture closing and housekeeping
topics.groupedBecause: This topic provides the concluding remarks, linking back to the learning outcomes and outlining upcoming practical sessions.
